units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, issued 05:30 ST
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a grey start with mist over inshore waters, slowly lifting to low cloud by midday. Light south-easterly winds, force 2 to 3. Maximum 8 C. Tonight: fog forming widely over the Sound and low ground after dusk, locally dense near Gilliver and Lisle. Minimum 4 C. Outlook: an extended spell of slack winds and fog patches through the coming days.

units.title: Fog advisory: Marrow Sound and coastal roads
units.author: met
units.text: Fog advisory valid from 18:00 ST today until 11:00 ST tomorrow. Visibility is expected to fall below 200 m over the Sound and coastal roads, and below 50 m in places. Drivers on the Port Ammet to Gilliver coast road should allow extra time and use dipped headlights. Small craft are advised to stay in harbour unless equipped with radar.

units.title: Tides and inshore waters
units.author: met
units.text: High water Port Ammet 05:12 (4.1 m) and 17:38 (4.3 m). Low water 11:27 and 23:51. Gilliver times are about 12 minutes later. Inshore waters: wind south-east 2 to 3, sea slight, visibility moderate becoming very poor in fog this evening. Neap tides through the weekend.

units.title: Sound Lines: morning service update
units.author: ferry
units.text: The 07:10 departure from Port Ammet left 25 minutes late after mist on the Lisle approach. Onward sailings to Gilliver are running about 20 minutes behind. We expect to recover the timetable by the 11:00 sailing. Thank you for your patience, and please arrive at the terminal at the usual time.

units.title: Sound Lines: evening and night sailings
units.author: ferry
units.text: With fog forecast this evening, evening and night crossings may run at reduced speed under restricted-visibility procedure. Please allow up to 30 minutes extra on the Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver route. Foot passengers waiting on the Lisle and Gilliver slips are asked to stay behind the barrier until the crew lower the ramp.

units.title: Notice to mariners: restricted visibility
units.author: coast
units.text: Mariners are reminded of the collision regulations on sound signals and safe speed in restricted visibility. The automated fog signal at Carrow Point will operate whenever visibility at the station falls below 2 nautical miles. Vessels on passage between Lisle and Gilliver should keep a listening watch on the harbour channel.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Gilliver approach buoy unlit
units.author: coast
units.text: The port-hand marker buoy on the Gilliver approach, number 3, is reported unlit. A repair visit is planned when conditions allow. Until then mariners should navigate with caution and should not rely on the light. Reported by the Gilliver harbourmaster on the morning of day 4.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby, Mill Lane area
units.author: power
units.text: Planned maintenance on the overhead line serving Mill Lane, Kiln Row and the eastern end of Tollinby market square, 09:00 to 13:00 ST today. Around 140 properties will be without power during the work. Customers who rely on powered medical equipment should call the priority line before 08:30.

units.title: Supply restored: Port Ammet north
units.author: power
units.text: A short interruption affected parts of Port Ammet north between 06:12 and 06:31 ST. Supply was restored automatically after a protective reclose. Engineers found a bird strike on the Hythe Road line. No further work is needed. We apologise for any inconvenience to early risers.

units.title: Waste collections: winter changes
units.author: council
units.text: Garden waste collections have now ended for the winter and will restart in spring. Recycling rounds in Rope Walk, Chandler Street and the Marsh Road estate move from Thursday to Friday for the next three weeks while a vehicle is repaired. Please put containers out by 07:00 on the new day.

units.title: Roads: Brackwater junction temporary signals
units.author: council
units.text: Temporary traffic signals at the Brackwater junction on the Tollinby road will stay in place while drainage work continues. The contractor expects to finish within the agreed period. The signals are on a fixed cycle and are not linked to sensors, so waits at quiet times are expected.

units.title: Planning: weekly list of delegated decisions
units.author: council
units.text: Decisions issued this week under delegated powers include: ADC/HH/0912, single-storey rear extension, 14 Kiln Row, Tollinby, approved; ADC/VEG/0917, total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm, determined, conditions as previously published; ADC/ADV/0921, illuminated fascia sign, Harbour Parade, Port Ammet, refused. Full documents are available at the council offices.

units.title: Evening update: fog thickening
units.author: met
units.text: Fog is now widespread over the Marrow Sound. Observed visibility at 19:00 ST: Gilliver 80 m, Lisle 150 m, Port Ammet harbour 300 m, Carrow Point 60 m. Little change expected overnight. Temperatures near the dew point everywhere, so windscreens and decks will be wet.

units.title: Sound Lines: night sailing delayed
units.author: ferry
units.text: The 22:40 sailing from Lisle to Gilliver is running about 35 minutes late because of dense fog in the channel. The return crossing to Port Ammet will leave Gilliver once the vessel has turned round. Passengers are asked to wait in the shelter rather than on the slip.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, issued 05:30 ST
units.author: met
units.text: Today: fog slow to clear and may persist all day over the Sound and at Gilliver. Inland, low cloud lifting to brighter spells around Tollinby this afternoon. Winds light and variable. Maximum 7 C. Tonight: fog reforming quickly after dusk, freezing fog possible in sheltered valleys around Brackwater. Minimum 2 C.

units.title: Road weather: freezing fog risk inland
units.author: met
units.text: Freezing fog is possible tonight in the Brackwater valley and on the reservoir road, where road surface temperatures may fall to minus 1 C. Untreated surfaces could become slippery after midnight. The council gritting service has been informed. Coastal roads should stay above freezing but remain foggy.

units.title: Inshore waters and tides
units.author: met
units.text: High water Port Ammet 05:58 (4.0 m) and 18:21 (4.1 m). Low water 12:10. Wind variable 1 to 2. Sea smooth. Visibility very poor in fog, occasionally moderate this afternoon between Lisle and Port Ammet. Fog banks are likely to be thickest close to the Holm and the Gilliver shore.

units.title: Sound Lines: 06:20 Lisle sailing cancelled
units.author: ferry
units.text: The 06:20 sailing from Lisle to Port Ammet is cancelled because visibility at the Lisle slip is below our operating limit. Passengers holding tickets for this sailing may travel on the 07:30, which will call at Lisle on the way from Gilliver. We are sorry for the disruption to early commuters.

units.title: Sound Lines: safety on the slipways
units.author: ferry
units.text: A reminder that the Gilliver and Lisle slipways are working areas. Members of the public should not walk to the end of the slip at any time, and especially not after dark or in fog, when crews may not see them during approach. Please use the shelters and wait for the boarding announcement.

units.title: Notice to mariners: drifting fishing gear
units.author: coast
units.text: Several creel marker buoys and a length of floating rope have been reported adrift between the Gilliver approach and the Kittering Holm shore. Vessels should keep a lookout, particularly in poor visibility. Owners who have lost gear may contact the Gilliver harbour office.

units.title: Small craft advisory: fog
units.author: coast
units.text: Owners of small craft without radar are advised not to put to sea in the Marrow Sound until the fog lifts. Kayakers and rowers should not attempt the Lisle crossing. The coastguard has dealt with two calls in the past 24 hours from craft unable to find the harbour entrance. Both were assisted safely.

units.title: Planned work: Brackwater village
units.author: power
units.text: Engineers will replace a pole-mounted transformer on Reservoir Lane, Brackwater, between 10:00 and 12:30 ST. Around 60 properties, including the reservoir visitor car park lighting, will be without power during the work. We expect to restore supply on time.

units.title: Fault: Gilliver Harbour Road street lighting
units.author: power
units.text: Four street lights on Harbour Road, Gilliver, between the chandlery and the slipway, are out following a cable fault. The council's lighting contractor has been asked to attend. Domestic supplies are not affected. Please take care on the harbour front after dark.

units.title: Water: Lisle Road main repair
units.author: council
units.text: A burst water main on Lisle Road, Port Ammet, will be repaired today. The road will be closed between the roundabout and Ferry Lane from 09:30 until about 15:00. Some homes may notice low pressure or cloudy water afterwards, which will clear if you run the cold tap for a few minutes.

units.title: Waste collections: fog delays
units.author: council
units.text: Fog this morning delayed rounds leaving the Marsh Road depot. Some collections in Port Ammet south and Gilliver may be completed later than usual today or tomorrow. If your bin has not been emptied by 18:00, please leave it out and crews will return. There is no need to report it.

units.title: Libraries: winter opening hours
units.author: council
units.text: From next week, Tollinby and Port Ammet libraries will close at 18:00 on weekdays instead of 19:00. Saturday hours are unchanged. The mobile library will continue to visit Gilliver and Brackwater every other Wednesday, weather permitting. Returns can still be left in the external box.

units.title: Sound Lines: night crossings tonight
units.author: ferry
units.text: Night crossings will run tonight under restricted-visibility procedure. Expect delays of 20 to 40 minutes on all legs after 21:00. The 23:15 departure from Gilliver will wait for connecting passengers from the Lisle bus if the bus is held by fog on the coast road.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, issued 05:30 ST
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a third day of fog over the Sound, with only brief clearances near Port Ammet around midday. High pressure remains centred to the north-east, keeping winds very light. Maximum 6 C. Tonight: dense fog again, locally freezing inland. Outlook: little change until a weak front arrives from the west in three or four days.

units.title: Fog advisory extended
units.author: met
units.text: The fog advisory for the Marrow Sound and coastal roads is extended until further notice. Overnight visibility at Carrow Point fell to 40 m and stayed below 100 m for nine hours. Drivers, cyclists and walkers on unlit roads should wear something light or reflective. Fog lights should be switched off once visibility improves.

units.title: Tides and inshore waters
units.author: met
units.text: High water Port Ammet 06:41 (3.9 m) and 19:02 (4.0 m). Low water 00:35 and 12:55. Wind light and variable. Sea smooth. Visibility very poor in fog, at times less than 100 m. Air temperature close to sea temperature, so fog over the water will be slow to lift.

units.title: Sound Lines: delays continue
units.author: ferry
units.text: All sailings today are expected to run late while fog persists. The timetable remains in force, but please check the bulletin before travelling. Vehicle bookings will be honoured on any sailing today. Our terminal at Port Ammet has extra seating and hot drinks available in the waiting room.

units.title: Sound Lines: freight and charter notice
units.author: ferry
units.text: Freight sailings and contracted supply runs from Port Ammet are being rescheduled around the passenger timetable while crossings are slow. Operators with standing charters will be contacted directly by the freight desk. Departures may move by up to two hours, depending on visibility at the destination.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Carrow Point fog signal
units.author: coast
units.text: The automated fog signal at Carrow Point operated continuously for 14 hours overnight. Residents near the headland have asked whether the signal can be reduced; it cannot, as it is a statutory aid to navigation. Mariners should note that the signal can be hard to locate by ear in still, dense fog.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Gilliver buoy update
units.author: coast
units.text: The repair visit to Gilliver approach buoy number 3 has been postponed because of fog. The buoy remains unlit. A temporary lit dan buoy will not be laid until the work boat can operate safely. Mariners should continue to navigate with caution in the approach.

units.title: Unplanned outage: Lisle west
units.author: power
units.text: Around 220 properties in Lisle west lost power from 05:48 ST after a fault on an underground cable joint. Engineers crossed on the first ferry and restored most customers by 09:20 using a temporary link. The remaining 11 properties should be reconnected by early afternoon.

units.title: Supply restored: Lisle west
units.author: power
units.text: All customers in Lisle west were reconnected by 13:40 ST. A permanent repair to the cable joint will be scheduled next week with notice given to affected households. If you are still without power, please check your trip switch before calling us.

units.title: Planning: public access to documents
units.author: council
units.text: The council has received a number of enquiries about decided applications. Planning decisions, conditions and officer reports are public documents. They can be viewed at the Port Ammet council offices on weekdays from 09:00 to 16:30, or on the council's planning pages. Copies circulating elsewhere may be incomplete or out of date.

units.title: Harbours: Gilliver slipway surface works
units.author: council
units.text: Minor resurfacing at the head of the Gilliver slipway is planned for next week, subject to weather. The ferry ramp area will stay open. A section of the public walkway beside the slip will be fenced off for about three days. Thank you to the harbour office for coordinating the work with the ferry timetable.

units.title: Waste collections: catch-up rounds
units.author: council
units.text: Crews completed most of yesterday's delayed rounds this morning. A small number of streets in Gilliver will be collected tomorrow. We know some residents in Rope Walk were missed again and apologise; the round has been added to the catch-up list.

units.title: Evening update: dense fog
units.author: met
units.text: Observed visibility at 19:00 ST: Gilliver 50 m, Lisle 90 m, Port Ammet harbour 200 m, Carrow Point 40 m, Brackwater reservoir 30 m in freezing fog. Air temperature 3 C at the coast and minus 1 C inland. The fog is expected to persist through the night and much of tomorrow.

units.title: Sound Lines: night service tonight
units.author: ferry
units.text: Night crossings will operate tonight with reduced speed. The 22:40 from Lisle and the 23:15 from Gilliver are expected to depart up to 45 minutes late. Waiting passengers at Gilliver are asked to use the harbour shelter, as the street lights by the slip remain out.
